openings.claim: Speculative capability: a removable floating edge cage could keep the hatch registered under sideways pull even when the right contact is raised, without tightening the seal into the observed corner-lift mode.
openings.delta: Change lateral registration from downward clamping friction to geometric edge stops carried by two removable rim yokes. Bolt the four strips into two rubber-padded pairs; use the straps for separation retention and cord to recover detached pieces. Allow vertical movement at the hatch-facing stops. The nearest rival is strap retention with increased corner pressure and no positive lateral stops.
openings.prediction: If accessible rim and hatch edges support this geometry, the cage should remain within 1 mm under 20 N across ten closures, including the final right-card disturbance. The rival should require greater pressure or permit greater sliding. Record sliding and opposite-corner lift separately: identical results leave the mechanism advantage unresolved.
openings.probe: First measure edge access, strap routing length and achievable stop clearance with ruler; abandon this geometry if the supplied parts cannot fit without altering the hatch, rim or seal. Allocate two closure/pull trials to the rival, one disturbed, and ten to the cage, with the final closure disturbed. Mark position, measure displacement under the scale, measure corner lift, time each reopening and inspect the seal. Remove or swing every carrier outside the marked opening before inspecting. Defeat the candidate if displacement exceeds 1 mm, reopening exceeds 30 seconds, a carrier escapes retention, the opening remains obstructed, the seal tears, or adequate registration requires corner tightening.
assumptions: Rim profile, edge access, hatch thickness, strap attachment and usable carrier clearance are unknown; these indispensable dependencies may prevent fabrication.
The supplied strips can provide stops without forcing the disturbed hatch flat; fabrication must fit ninety minutes and observation twenty minutes.
No load capacity or successful cycle result is established; this is an enabling probe, not deployment.

assessment: One live opening; feasibility depends on unprovided rim geometry. Supplied sliding and corner lift motivate separating lateral registration from seal preload; neither proves the proposed cage works.
